problem:
Evaluate the triple integral

$$
{∭}_{R}\frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}}\,\text{d}V
$$

over the region $R$ enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=16.$

activity_context.topic_title: Triple Integrals in Spherical Polar Coordinates

examples.knowledge_point: Evaluating a Triple Integral by Converting to Spherical Polar Coordinates
examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14096572/assets/48a7c7ea2614c0b46df169cf353183f5b862f5feabab97a050107fe227f1521a.png)

 

Evaluate the triple integral

$$
\displaystyle \iiint\limits_R 2z\sqrt{x^2 + y^2 + z^2} \:\textrm{d}V
$$

over the region $R$ enclosed inside the sphere $x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = 9$ for $y \leq 0,$ shown above.
examples.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
\iiint\limits_{R} f(x,y,z) \, \mathrm{d}V = 

\iiint\limits_{\Delta} \, f(\rho\cos\theta\sin\phi, \rho\sin\theta\sin\phi, \rho\cos\phi) \:  \rho^2\sin\phi \: \mathrm{d}\rho \, \mathrm{d}\theta \, \mathrm{d}\phi.
$$

If $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x = \rho\cos\theta\sin\phi, \qquad

y = \rho\sin\theta\sin\phi, \qquad 

z = \rho\cos\phi
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents one-half of the sphere of radius $3$ centered at the origin.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14096572/assets/cd2f48915774902314c38f2b5e40baa646761ae14b560eab401d8841f61f5612.png)

 

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
\Delta = \left\{ (\rho, \theta, \phi) \, : \, 0 \leq \rho \leq 3, \: \pi \leq \theta \leq 2\pi, \: 0 \leq \phi \leq \pi \right\}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z) = 2z\sqrt{x^2 + y^2 + z^2}{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =2\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\cdot \rho  \\  & =2{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}2z\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}2{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{3}{\rho }^{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡2ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡2ϕ\,dϕ\cdot {\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }d\theta \cdot {\int }_{0}^{3}{\rho }^{4}\,d\rho  \\  & ={[-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡2ϕ]}_{ϕ=0}^{ϕ=\pi }\cdot [\theta ]_{\theta =\pi }^{\theta =2\pi }\cdot {[\frac{1}{5}{\rho }^{5}]}_{\rho =0}^{\rho =3} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}(1-1)\cdot (2\pi -\pi )\cdot \frac{1}{5}(243-0) \\  & =0\cdot \pi \cdot \frac{243}{5} \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14096572/assets/0aadb414e61f8a7e9d1ba1d47e10c2ba1e7b94b72155c0882a08e0121646f6f6.png)

The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=-12z,$ shown above. 
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}\frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}\,\text{d}V
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents the sphere of radius $6$ centered at $(0,0,-6).$

With that in mind, let's now write the ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=-12z$ in spherical polar coordinates:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2} & =-12z \\ {\rho }^{2} & =-12\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ \\ \rho (\rho +12\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since $\rho $ cannot be identical to zero on the entire sphere, we must have $\rho =-12\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14096572/assets/a303436877fdc4559e7bdfc302f8660258ea6ee3cb46d9adb0eb961a1e889b27.png)

 

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ={(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le -12\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ,\,0\le \theta \le 2\pi ,\,\frac{\pi }{2}\le ϕ\le \pi }.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)^{2}+(\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{{\rho }^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{{\rho }^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}\frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}\frac{1}{\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{-12\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ}\rho \,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$
